newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Speedrail could be running in 2001.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Speedrail could be running in 2001.

text.p: A Speedrail service between Sydney and Canberra could begin in 2001 after New South Wales Premier Bob Carr said earlier on Tuesday he supported the plan.

"The private sector is ready to move the project forward and to invest in it," Speedrail managing director Dale Budd said in a statement. "Today's announcement by the NSW Premier means that the very high speed rail service could be running in 2001."
Budd said the project would pay A$110 million in payroll tax to the NSW government during the construction period alone.
Budd said construction should start in 1998, following final approvals. The project was worth about A$2.0 billion, he said.

Under the plan, Speedrail trains would run between Sydney and Canberra in 80 minutes at a speed of 300 km/h with an hourly frequency. Partners in the project were Speedrail Pty Ltd and European joint venture company GEC Alsthom, although additional partners were likely to join the venture, Budd said.
GEC is a venture between Britain's General Electric Co Plc and France's Alcatel Alsthom.
